skill.name: email-deliverability-specialist
skill.description: Diagnose email authentication, bounces, spam placement, sender reputation, consent and unsubscribe problems. Use for deliverability audits, safe remediation plans and sender-platform capability checks, not general campaign copywriting.
skill.summary: Diagnose deliverability problems and plan evidence-based fixes for authentication, reputation, consent and unsubscribe workflows.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

finding_verdicts.reason: The SMTP identity appears in a synthetic authentication example, not a sending operation. The evaluation instructions explicitly prohibit sending, DNS changes and account access.
SMTP MAIL FROM is a header identity to inspect during authentication diagnosis, not an instruction to send mail. The paragraph also requires trusted receiver provenance.
The reference explicitly states that private keys never belong in DNS or chat. It requests public DKIM records and documents safe key rotation.
TXT record checks and include tracing diagnose public SPF policies for the sender under review. The guidance preserves legitimate senders and rejects unsafe policy changes.
This paragraph explains DMARC domain alignment and organizational-domain matching. It contains no host enumeration, system access or reconnaissance instructions.
The paragraph links a public consent guide and requires verification of product claims against account capabilities. It rejects unsupported recommendations and promotional links.
The instruction preserves SMTP replies and timestamps for diagnosing existing delivery failures. It does not initiate messages or request external transmission.
Collecting delivery status and sending identity is relevant evidence for the requested email diagnosis. No system probing or unrelated information collection is instructed.
The paragraph requires honoring opt-outs, preserving suppression information and separating transactional messages from marketing. These are consent safeguards, not system reconnaissance.
The workflow measures subscription eligibility and tests integrations with synthetic contacts. It explicitly discourages unnecessary data collection and contains no system probing.
The skill requests relevant sender configuration and redacted diagnostic artifacts, not permission to send mail. Its workflow separately requires authorization for sends and configuration changes.

content.value_statement: Email authentication failures, filtering and consent gaps can hide behind successful delivery reports. This skill turns diagnostic evidence into prioritized findings and reversible remediation plans.
actual_capabilities: Analyze SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment using receiver headers, DNS evidence and sending configuration.
Distinguish SMTP deferrals, permanent rejections, server acceptance and inbox placement.
Review consent provenance, suppression synchronization and one-click unsubscribe behavior.
Compare mailbox-provider requirements and verify platform capabilities against primary documentation.
Prepare prioritized remediation plans with ownership, approval requirements, rollback steps and verification criteria.
Design evidence-based reputation recovery plans without fixed warm-up schedules or enforcement evasion.
limitations: Live DNS, browser and account checks depend on tools and permissions available in the host environment.
The skill provides guidance, not a bundled email sender or automatic DNS deployment tool.
It cannot guarantee inbox placement, reputation recovery deadlines or legal compliance.
Provider requirements and platform capabilities require current verification; supplied references are not permanent guarantees.

use_cases.title: Investigate Authentication Failures
use_cases.description: Reconcile receiver headers with sender configuration and public DNS to identify alignment failures and prepare controlled changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Reputation Recovery
use_cases.description: Compare provider complaint metrics, list provenance and sending changes to contain affected traffic and define measurable recovery steps.

use_cases.title: Audit Subscription Workflows
use_cases.description: Trace permission status from signup through integrations, unsubscribe processing and suppression using authorized synthetic contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a Delivery Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Our [marketing or transactional] emails reach spam at [mailbox provider]. We use [platform]. Ask for essential redacted evidence and identify initial diagnostic steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish symptoms and collect evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Authentication Alignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these redacted receiver headers and DNS results: [artifacts]. Explain SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment. Separate observed facts from unknowns. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Consent and Unsubscribe
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [signup flow], [integration] and [unsubscribe evidence]. Check eligibility, one-click headers and suppression synchronization. Propose synthetic tests and identify required approvals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate collection and unsubscribe behavior across systems.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Controlled Recovery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [redacted provider metrics], [SMTP errors], [sender inventory] and [recent changes], build a prioritized recovery plan. Include denominators, hypotheses, owners, approvals, rollback and stopping criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate evidence-based remediation across providers and sending streams.

output_examples.input: Synthetic receiver results show SPF and DKIM passing for mailer.example.net, but DMARC failing for a visible From domain of example.com.
output: Observed: neither authenticated domain aligns with the visible From domain.
A second SPF record will not repair this alignment failure.
Verify platform support for aligned DKIM or a custom return path before proposing authorized changes.
Check new receiver results after implementation; authentication success does not guarantee inbox placement.

output_examples.input: An ESP reports 99% delivered and 0.1% complaints, while Yahoo reports 0.4% complaints. The team proposes doubling volume.
output: Server acceptance does not establish inbox placement.
Compare reporting windows and denominators before interpreting the complaint-rate difference.
Investigate consent sources, suppression behavior and recent sending changes.
Do not double volume without evidence supporting expansion; define provider-specific monitoring and stopping criteria.

output_examples.input: A synthetic marketing message has a body unsubscribe link, but no evidence of one-click headers or downstream suppression.
output: A body link alone does not establish RFC 8058 one-click support.
Inspect List-Unsubscribe, List-Unsubscribe-Post and DKIM coverage of both headers.
Test the POST flow only with an authorized synthetic subscriber.
Verify downstream suppression and processing time rather than relying only on endpoint success.

best_practices: Provide redacted receiver headers, timestamped DNS evidence and provider-specific metrics with clear denominators.
Require explicit approval before sending tests, changing DNS, editing suppressions or sharing reports externally.
Verify current primary documentation and use synthetic contacts to test complete workflows.
anti_patterns: Treating authentication passes or ESP acceptance as proof of inbox placement.
Removing suppressions, buying lists or rotating domains to bypass reputation enforcement.
Deploying invented DNS values or strict DMARC policies without sender inventory, approval and rollback.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex and Claude Code. Live checks depend on the tools and permissions available in each environment.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails or change DNS automatically?
faq.answer: It includes diagnostic instructions, not sending or deployment software. It requires authorization before campaign sends, DNS changes or account configuration.

faq.question: Can it diagnose problems without account access?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze supplied redacted artifacts and provide read-only collection steps. It must mark unavailable checks as unknown.

faq.question: Will passing SPF, DKIM and DMARC guarantee delivery?
faq.answer: No. Authentication does not guarantee inbox placement. Reputation, consent, filtering and recipient-provider policies remain relevant.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your sending platform, affected providers, sending domains, recent changes and representative errors. Redact recipient data and never share private keys or credentials.

faq.question: Does it certify legal or provider compliance?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify evidence and requirements, but legal obligations and provider rules require current, context-specific verification.
